subject: Staged failover SLA variance request — temporary RTO/RPO adjustment during region maintenance
messages:
From: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@gpbank.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@gpbank.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jul 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Staged failover during datacenter maintenance — RTO/RPO clarification

David —

Quick follow-up from our security review: Greenpoint is planning a network and storage maintenance in us-east-1 over the weekend of July 18–19. We understand Redwood offers multi-region failover, but we need written confirmation on two items for our internal risk board before we finalize the procurement paperwork:

1) During a planned maintenance-induced standby activation (staged failover where traffic is incrementally routed to warm standbys), what is Redwood's committed RTO and RPO?
2) Are temporary variances permitted for a 48h maintenance window (we need to know if you can guarantee RPO <= 2 hours and RTO <= 30 minutes during that window, or whether a carveout is required)?

If a formal carveout is needed, please propose compensating controls (e.g., prioritized routing, read-only replicas, parity cache warming) and any liability adjustments. We need language to present to compliance.

Thanks —
Oliver
Security Architect
Greenpoint Bank

Attachments: GPB_Security_QA.pdf

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@gpbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jul 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staged failover during datacenter maintenance — RTO/RPO clarification

Hi Oliver —

Thanks for flagging this. Short answers up front:
- For normal (non-maintenance) events with our standard multi-region configuration we publish an RTO of 15 minutes and an effective RPO of under 15 minutes for active/passive with continuous cross-region replication.
- For planned staged failover scenarios tied to provider maintenance, we sometimes recommend a temporary variance if customers require extended lead times for runbook coordination (particularly when on-prem connectors or partner network changes are involved).

Proposed approach for the July 18–19 window:
- We can commit to an RTO target of 30 minutes and an RPO target of 2 hours for a limited, documented variance window, provided the mitigation checklist below is accepted by Greenpoint:
  * Redwood will perform prefix cache warming and prioritize GPB traffic on warm standbys for the 6h pre-window.
  * GPB will accept a temporary read-only mode for certain low-priority endpoints during the maintenance window (details below).
  * Redwood will provide a dedicated on-call SRE during the window and a direct pager channel to GPB SRE.
- Liability: Redwood proposes a temporary SLA carveout document limited to the maintenance window with a service credit cap (to be detailed) instead of permanent SLA changes.

I'm looping Marissa for the operational commitments and Monica for the legal/contract language. Naomi — can you confirm capacity availability for a prioritized warm standby on those dates?

Best,
David
Head of Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0123

Attachment: redwood-staged-failover-runbook-v2.docx

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 9 Jul 2025 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staged failover during datacenter maintenance — RTO/RPO clarification

Oliver / David —

Operational notes from the runbook perspective:

1) Staged failover flow (summary):
- T-minus 6h: initiate KV cache prefix warming and trace rehydration, pre-populate model-specific KV shards for GPB routes.
- T-minus 1h: set GPB low-priority endpoints to read-only (non-critical write paths only) and start traffic shadowing to warm standby in us-west-2.
- Activation: route X% traffic every 5 minutes until full cutover; monitor latency and token-loss metrics.
- Rollback: automatic rollback if token-loss > 0.2% or p95 latency degradation beyond threshold.

2) RTO/RPO expectations:
- With the above steps and a dedicated warm pool, we expect practical RTO ~15–25 mins. RPO depends on whether GPB needs strict transactional durability for writes — for typical inference workloads we can maintain sub-30m RPO; for heavy write-throughput ingestion we recommend RPO=2h as a safe bound during staged operations.

3) Compensating controls we can implement now: prioritized routing, a temporary capacity reservation (small hourly charge), and an audit log export to GPB's S3 for the window.

I've attached the runbook draft. If GPB agrees to the read-only compromise for a subset of endpoints (list in the doc), we can avoid an SLA carveout entirely; otherwise we accept a time-boxed variance with a limited credit.

Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Attachment: standby-activation-heatmap.csv

Date: Thu, 10 Jul 2025 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staged failover during datacenter maintenance — RTO/RPO clarification

David / Marissa —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear runbook. We conferred with our risk board and operations: they prefer not to accept a permanent SLA change; a time-boxed variance with compensating controls is acceptable. Two asks before we approve:

1) Please provide the exact proposed service credit language (cap and calculation) for the 48h window.
2) Share the list of endpoints you propose to set read-only (we need to validate against our downstream payment queues).

If those two items are in the carveout doc by Monday 14 July we can sign off and proceed with a limited variance for July 18–19. I'll attach any follow-up notes from compliance after that.

Oliver
Security Architect
Greenpoint Bank
